findings.finding: The Q3 EPS bar ($1.08 EW / $1.09 others) sits about 4-5% below Q2 2026's reported $1.13, and Q2's drivers are documented as continuing: NII $58.3m (+6% y/y), total loans +$106m (+2%) q/q to $5.58bn with C&I +$65.6m, NIM 3.49% flat with management citing a steepening curve as a margin positive, provision $1.7m and net charge-offs $24k, efficiency improving q/q to 48.6%, and $51.9m of securities cash flow to redeploy into loans; a flat quarter prints ~$1.12-1.14, a beat against the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS is the line this name trades on: Q2 2026 beat by $0.05-0.06 (revenue missed) +3.67%; Q1 2026 record +3.12%; Q4 2025 record (+24% NI) +4.20%; Q3 2025 missed by ~1c -5.14% (https://www.tipranks.com/news/the-fly/lakeland-financial-eports-q3-eps-1-03-consensus-1-04-thefly). 5 of 7 baseline reactions up.
findings.why_not_priced: The bar was set below the last print rather than at it (analysts held ~$1.08-1.09 after a $1.13 quarter, possibly normalising Q2's near-zero charge-offs and lower provision). If the market expected ~$1.13 the published consensus would sit there and the stock would not be 7% below its early-August level with shorts building. Partly priced: the Q2 run-rate is public, so this is sized below the name's median reaction.
findings.independence: Peer margins and credit in the same footprint (finding 2, separate documents) point the same way; nothing confirms LKFN's own Q3 number.

findings.finding: Indiana peers that reported Q3 2026 after LKFN last spoke show stable-to-rising margins and clean credit: 1st Source (South Bend, same northern-Indiana footprint) NIM 4.28% FTE +4bp q/q, NCOs 0.02%, NPAs down to 0.81% from 1.01%, EPS $2.03 +18.7% y/y; First Merchants NIM 3.44% +6bp q/q; Old National NIM -2bp to 3.52% with total deposit cost +8bp to 1.79% on funding competition.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: LKFN's NIM moved from 3.50% (Q3 2025) to 3.49% (Q1, Q2 2026); the Q3 2025 print with NIM at the 3.50% peak still fell -5.14% on the EPS miss, so margin alone has not driven the reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: These releases landed 21-22 October, after LKFN's last communication, and LKFN's three-analyst consensus may not have been refreshed for them; if it had, the bar would have drifted toward the Q2 actual. A proxy: transmission to LKFN's own deposit mix (seasonal public funds, brokered deposits) is unconfirmed, and Old National's deposit-cost rise cuts the other way, so sized small.
findings.independence: First Merchants 8-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000712534/000071253426000073/a3q26earningsreleaseex991.htm (2026-10-21); Old National 8-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000707179/000162828026066598/onb_exhibit991er3q26.htm (2026-10-21). Proxies, not LKFN data.

findings.finding: The FOMC raised the funds target 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-17, the first hike in over three years; LKFN describes a neutral rate posture, so the Q3 effect is about two weeks and small, while Regions said lagged retail deposit repricing should lift Q4 NII - any LKFN Q4 margin commentary is the forward line this could move.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: LKFN gives no numeric guidance; qualitative margin commentary accompanied the +3.67% Q2 reaction. No history of reacting to a rate-move commentary specifically.
findings.why_not_priced: Macro is public and priced in the sector; what is not public is LKFN's own read of the hike on its Q4 margin. With a neutral posture the expected sign is near zero, hence the small size.
findings.independence: Regions Q3 2026 release/transcript on lagged repricing lifting Q4 NII: https://www.earningswhispers.com/transcript/RF (proxy).

findings.finding: Short interest has built into the print: 2,484,880 shares at 2026-09-30 (about 10% of shares outstanding, 11.0 days to cover) against 2,173,782 at 2026-07-31 and 1,907,859 at 2026-05-29, on a name whose bar sits below its last quarter; a clean beat meets a crowded short with 11 days of volume to cover.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The short has been near or above ~2m shares through the last three prints, all of which rose +3.1% to +4.2% on beats; the one miss (Q3 2025) fell -5.14%.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is public but the options market is dead (OI 15), so no one prices the squeeze through the chain; the stock 7% off its August level with shorts rising is what a priced negative looks like, leaving the upside asymmetric on a beat. The short may also reflect an informed credit view (finding 5), which is why this is not sized larger.
findings.independence: none (single data source for the register; same fact as positioning_check)

findings.finding: Credit tail: LKFN's watch list and individually analyzed loans rose $15.7m (+9%) in Q2 to $198.0m (3.55% of loans, from 3.33% in Q1), with ~$13.2m of downgrades and three relationships totalling ~$24.7m moved to individual analysis; Q2 2025 carried a $28.9m partial charge-off on one credit, and First Merchants took $29.4m of Q3 2026 charge-offs on two commercial credits in the same state.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2025 print that carried the $28.9m partial charge-off (2025-07-25 in the baseline) still rose +2.74%, so this name has looked through a large single-credit charge-off before; the Q3 2025 EPS miss cost -5.14%.
findings.why_not_priced: The watch-list rise is public since July, so the level is partly priced (and the short build may be this view); what is not priced is whether any of the $24.7m moved to individual analysis needs a reserve or charge-off in Q3. Management said mid-year reviews found no significant concerns, and the crowded short shrinks this negative.
findings.independence: Same document as finding 1 (two readings of the Q2 release, opposite lines: run-rate vs credit tail). First Merchants' Q3 charge-offs (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000712534/000071253426000073/a3q26earningsreleaseex991.htm) are a regional proxy; 1st Source's falling NPAs (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/34782/000003478226000054/ex09302026991pressrelease1.htm) point the other way.

findings.finding: The only revenue consensus found ($73.65m, Earnings Whispers) is ~3.9% above Q2's reported $70.9m, which itself 'missed'; Q2 NII $58.3m plus ~$12.6m noninterest income would need ~$2.8m of q/q growth, so a headline revenue miss alongside an EPS beat is likely again.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 had exactly this combination (EPS beat, revenue miss: https://finviz.com/news/372874/lakeland-financial-posts-earnings-beat-despite-revenue-shortfall) and rose +3.67%, so the revenue line has not been punished.
findings.why_not_priced: Single-source bar with an unclear definition (likely FTE or gross of something), so capped small; if the market cared about this line Q2's revenue miss would have shown in the reaction.

findings.finding: Capital return is steady and in place: the board declared an unchanged $0.52 quarterly dividend on 2026-10-13 (raises come in January: +4% in Jan 2026), and Q2 bought back 70,873 shares at $58.20 with $17.1m of authority left to 2027-04-30 - the stock is back at that buyback price ($58.78).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No history of capital-return news moving the print; buyback disclosure is routine in each release.
findings.why_not_priced: Dividend is public and unchanged (no information); a larger Q3 buyback at ~$58-60 would be disclosed only in the release, a small positive at most.
